title: What Is Computer Vision?
introduction: Computer vision lets machines look at pictures and videos and understand what they see. It is the foundation for many everyday AI tools, from photo apps to self‑driving cars.

sections.heading: Defining Computer Vision
paragraphs: Computer vision is a field of artificial intelligence that enables computers to interpret visual information such as images and video.
It works by converting visual data into numbers that algorithms can analyze, just like our brain processes light into thoughts.

example.title: Smartphone Photo Tagging
example.content: When you open a photo gallery, the app can suggest tags like "beach" or "birthday" by recognizing patterns in the picture.

sections.heading: How AI Interprets Images
paragraphs: An image is made of tiny dots called pixels, each with a color value. AI models read these values and look for patterns.
The model learns from many labeled examples, so it can later predict what new images contain.

example.title: Handwritten Digit Recognition
example.content: A simple AI can look at a photo of a handwritten number and correctly say whether it is a 0, 1, 2, etc., by comparing pixel patterns to its training data.

sections.heading: Image Classification
paragraphs: Image classification assigns a single label to an entire picture, such as "cat" or "car".
The model examines the whole image and chooses the most likely category based on what it has learned.

example.title: Animal Photo Organizer
example.content: A program can scan a folder of pet photos and automatically place all cat pictures in one album and dog pictures in another.

sections.heading: Object Detection
sections.subheading: Finding and locating items in pictures
paragraphs: Object detection not only labels what is in an image but also draws boxes around each item.
It tells the computer both the type of object and where it is located in the picture.

example.title: Self‑Driving Car Pedestrian Detection
example.content: The car’s camera system spots pedestrians, draws a box around each person, and alerts the vehicle to stop or slow down.

sections.heading: Real‑World Vision Applications
paragraphs: Retail stores use vision to track items on shelves and speed up checkout without scanning barcodes.
Healthcare uses vision to examine X‑rays and detect anomalies early.

example.title: Barcode‑Free Checkout
example.content: A camera looks at the items you place on the counter, identifies each product, and totals the price automatically.

practice.title: Simple Image Classification Exercise
practice.instruction: Pick three everyday objects (for example, an apple, a shoe, and a book). Take a photo of each or find pictures online. Write down the category you think each picture belongs to, then compare your list with how a phone’s photo app tags them.

keyTakeaways: Computer vision enables machines to understand images and video.
Image classification gives a single label to an entire picture, while object detection also finds the location of each object.
Computer vision powers many real‑world tools such as photo tagging, self‑driving cars, retail checkout, and medical imaging.

mcqs.question: What is the primary purpose of computer vision?
options: Enable computers to interpret visual information such as images and video
Allow computers to process audio signals
mcqs.explanation: Computer vision is defined as the field that lets machines understand visual data like pictures and videos.

mcqs.question: How many labels does image classification assign to a picture?
mcqs.explanation: Image classification gives a single, most likely category label to the whole image.

mcqs.question: Which description matches object detection?
options: Assigns a single label to the whole image
Draws bounding boxes around each identified object and labels them
mcqs.explanation: Object detection not only tells what objects are present but also shows where they are by drawing boxes.

mcqs.question: How does an AI model learn to recognize handwritten digits?
options: By reading a dictionary of words
By analyzing audio recordings of people speaking numbers
By being trained on many labeled examples of digit images
mcqs.explanation: The model is trained on a large set of labeled digit images, allowing it to compare pixel patterns and make predictions.

mcqs.question: Which real‑world application uses computer vision to identify products without scanning barcodes?
mcqs.explanation: Barcode‑free checkout relies on cameras to recognize items on the counter, a direct use of computer vision.
